p.i: Vir Clariss. Disputationem tuam de Magistratu Politico adversus Bell. eò diligentius legi, quò videre potui, eam accuratius esse conscriptam, & deprehendi non tantum argumentorum gravissimorum veritate, sed & Clariss. Theologorum authoritate undecumque suffultam ac munitam. Non dubito, quin rem gratiss. feceris iis, qui materiam hanc accuratius pernoscere cupiunt. Me certè tibi devinctum hoc nomine habes, & quia nos pudere non debet profiteri, per quem profecerimus, fateor me tra-ctatu hoc tuo doctiss. in iis, in quibus fluctuabam ante, expeditum & quae ne-sciebam, edoctum.Deus tibi sufficiat porrò vires ad bene merendum de Ecclesia Dei.

page.notes: No doubtful readings. "edoctum.Deus" is printed with no space after the stop; left as printed. The large initial V is joined to "Ir" as "Vir". The text is set in italic throughout, apart from the closing lines, which are roman. The "Digitized by Google" stamp at the bottom right is left out.
